```{r}
pharma<-read.csv("Pharmaceuticals.csv")
 row.names(pharma)<-pharma$Symbol
num<- pharma[, 3:11]
str(num)
```
```{r}
library(cluster)
z <- scale(num)
round(apply(z, 2, sd), 2)
```
#a. k means gets its data by distance so any large numbers would causle an outlier. I made everything have an equal variable whieght so that nothing cause z scores or k- means to cause a skew in the data.
```{r}

set.seed(1)
clustersum <-sapply(1:7, function(k) kmeans(z, centers = k, nstart=50)$tot.withinss)
plot(1:7, clustersum, type ="b", pch = 19,
     xlab = "# of clusters", ylab ="total inside cluste ", 
     main= "Elbow plot")
```
```{r}
d <- dist(z)
set.seed(1)
avg<- sapply(2:7, function(k){
  Kmen<- kmeans(z, centers = k,nstart =51)
  mean(silhouette(Kmen$cluster, d)[, "sil_width"])
})
```
# THe plot shows a downward slop that is conststent across. it shows a decrease as you increase clustes.

```{r}
plot(2:7, avg, type ="b", pch = 19,
xlab="k", ylab ="Avg silh width", main ="silh")
round(avg,3)
```
# for k I choose 3 because it had the highest average shiloute score

```{r}
set.seed(1)
kMS<- kmeans(z, centers = 3, nstart =51)
kMS$size
pharma$Cluster<- kMS$cluster
split(rownames(pharma),pharma$Cluster)
```
```{r}
profile <-aggregate(num, by = list(Cluster = kMS$cluster), FUN = mean)
round(profile, 2)
round(kMS$centers, 2)
```
#bCLuster 1 market cap in the middle at 21.75  pe is the largest at 46.9. roe and roa are low. CLuster 2 has the larget cap at 97.1 The higest roe and roa and net profit of 20. THis company seems to be the most profitable
# cluster 3 is the middle it has the smallest market cap  and highest beta scor this apperas to be a small biz.

```{r}
matplot(t(kMS$centers), type = "l", lty= 1, lwd =2, col = 1:3, xaxt ="n",
        ylab = "STD mean", main = "profiles of cluster")
axis(1, at = 1:9, labels = colnames(num), las =2, cex.axis =.6)
legend("topright", legend = paste("Cluster", 1:3), col =1:4, lty =1, lwd =2)
       abline(h=0, lty = 2)
```
```{r}
table(pharma$Cluster, pharma$Median_Recommendation)
table(pharma$Cluster , pharma$Location)
table(pharma$Cluster, pharma$Exchange)
```
